sections.h2: What the Judge of Probate does in a home sale
sections.html:
The Judge of Probate in Jefferson County runs the recording office where deeds and mortgages become part of the public record. When a house sells, the deed goes to this office, the deed tax is collected, and the transfer shows up in the land records.

The same court handles estates, so an inherited house often passes through the same building twice, first for the estate and later for the sale. Employees can't give legal advice or prepare or revise a deed. Anyone who needs a deed drafted is pointed to an attorney.

Jefferson County has two probate divisions, Birmingham and Bessemer. Both work under the same Probate Judge, Deputy Probate Judge and Chief Clerk, and both keep hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., Monday through Friday.

DivisionCourthouse address
Birmingham716 North Richard Arrington Jr. Blvd., Birmingham, AL 35203
Bessemer1801 3rd Avenue North, Bessemer, AL 35020

Bessemer is about 16 miles by car southwest of Birmingham. If you're unsure which office to use, call the Probate Court at (205) 325-5203.

Jefferson County is the most populous county in Alabama, with 674,721 people in the 2020 census and a 2025 estimate of 665,742. Cities in the county include Birmingham, Bessemer, Hoover, Homewood, Vestavia Hills, Mountain Brook, Trussville, Gardendale, Fultondale, Hueytown, Pleasant Grove and Center Point.

Several of them reach across county lines. Birmingham, Hoover, Helena, Vestavia Hills, Leeds and Trussville all extend partly into a neighboring county, so check which county's records hold your parcel before you start. Recording a deed in the wrong county's office wastes time at closing.

The main state charge is a deed tax of 50 cents for each $500 of value, set by Code of Alabama section 40-22-1. A reduction applies when a mortgage on which the mortgage tax was already paid is part of the deal. Recording fees for the pages themselves come on top, and they vary by document.

A few more rules from the statute:

  • A deed must come with proof of the actual purchase price, using the Department of Revenue form.
  • If proof is withheld after a request, the penalty is $100 or 25 percent of the tax, whichever is greater.
  • Two thirds of the tax goes to the state treasury and one third to the county.
  • Deeds for nominal consideration meant only to perfect title carry no tax, and the office stamps them "No Tax Collected."

Ask the closing attorney or title company for the exact total on your settlement statement. Who pays the deed tax is set by the sales contract.

sections.h2: What the recording office can and can't tell you
sections.html:
Clerks can show you the public record, but they can't tell you whether a lien sits on your house. A title search is a job for a title company or attorney.

Records are open to the public online and in person. Subscribers to the LANDMARK WEB service can search land records and view images of select documents, and clerks offer free on-site training. Many documents can be viewed on the website at no charge, with uncertified printouts available for a small fee.

ServiceCost
Copies made in the Record Room$1.00 per page
Plat copies$15.00 per page
Certification of a copy$2.00 more per document

Payment can be made by credit card, cash, cashier's check, money order, business check or local personal check with identification.

sections.h2: What a Jefferson County seller should have ready
sections.html:
• The deed or estate paperwork showing how you took title.
  • A payoff statement for every mortgage on the house.
  • Government ID for everyone signing.
  • The sales contract, because the price drives the deed tax and the required value statement.
  • Any divorce decree or court order that affects title. Decrees are recorded and indexed with the land records, though not every court document is filed there.

A house owned by a deceased relative needs the estate sorted out first. The buyer's title company will want to see who has authority to sign.

sections.h2: From deed to property tax bill
sections.html:
Recording the deed is the first of three steps a new owner takes with the county. Record the deed in probate court, then have the property assessed in your name at the revenue office, then claim any exemption you qualify for.

Property taxes are due October 1 and delinquent after December 31. The bill follows the owner of record from the prior October 1, so the first bill after a sale can still carry the seller's name. If you get a bill after closing, send it to the title company or the buyer.

sections.h2: How a sale usually moves through the office
sections.html:
Most sales follow the same order. The buyer's title company or closing attorney drafts the deed and checks the record for liens. You sign at closing, and the deed is then taken to the probate office with the value statement and payment of the deed tax and recording fees. Once it is recorded, the transfer appears in the land records and the sale is public.

Because the clerks can't fix a deed, a mistake in a name or legal description has to go back to the attorney who drafted it. Ask for a copy of the recorded deed afterward and keep it with your closing papers.

sections.h2: Situations Jefferson County sellers often face
sections.html:
The county is large and varied, so the problems change with the neighborhood.

  • Older homes in former mill and mining communities such as Ensley, North Birmingham and Woodlawn, which were once separate towns and are now Birmingham neighborhoods.
  • Inherited houses where the heirs live out of state.
  • Parcels near county lines where it is unclear which probate office applies.
  • Vacant houses with unpaid tax or code issues.
  • Sellers who need to close fast and can't wait for a retail buyer's financing.

Cash Home Buyers makes written offers on Jefferson County houses as they stand. A local title company handles the recording at closing, so a cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and repair demands but still goes through the same probate office.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Jefferson County, Alabama?
faqs.a: Record it with the Probate Court of Jefferson County, at the Birmingham division (716 North Richard Arrington Jr. Blvd.) or the Bessemer division (1801 3rd Avenue North). Hours are 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., Monday through Friday.

faqs.q: How much is the Alabama deed tax?
faqs.a: Alabama charges 50 cents per $500 of value, or fraction of $500, under Code of Alabama section 40-22-1. A reduction applies when mortgage tax was already paid on a mortgage that stays with the property.

faqs.q: Can the Jefferson County probate office prepare my deed?
faqs.a: No. Employees may not prepare or revise a deed or give legal advice. Contact an attorney.

faqs.q: Can the recording office tell me if there is a lien on my house?
faqs.a: No. Clerks can't perform a title search, so a title company or attorney has to do it.

faqs.q: How much does a copy of a recorded deed cost?
faqs.a: Copies made in the Record Room are $1.00 per page, plats are $15.00 per page, and certification costs $2.00 more per document.
